punchline: A psychologist bought the best-fitting jeans of his life and walked out feeling worse about them.
thirty_sec: Barry Schwartz just wanted a pair of jeans. The shop asked him which fit, which cut, which wash. So he tried loads, and left with the best-fitting pair he'd ever owned. And he felt worse. All that choice had raised what he expected, so even great jeans fell short, and he blamed himself for picking wrong. His fix: decide what good enough looks like, and stop when you find it.
question: Have you ever made a choice that was perfectly fine but still felt disappointing because there were so many other options?
